en: The Auspicious Dawn of Viśvanātha of Kāśī.
I bow to Viśveśa, Mādhava, Dhundhi, Daṇḍapāṇi, and Bhairava; to Kāśī, Guhā, Gaṅgā, Bhavānī, and Maṇikarṇikā. 1.
Arise, O Kāśī! The Blessed Lord Viśvanātha is adorned with lotuses blessed by contact with the waves of the Gaṅgā;
and [O Goddess], you are accompanied by Annapūrṇā and the faces of Śrī Dhuṇḍhibhairava and others.
And your mother joyfully desires a fair dawn for you. 2.
Brahmā, the enemy of Mura (Viṣṇu), the destroyer of Tripura,
the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu.
May everyone on earth experience a beautiful dawn. 3.
O Gaṇeśa Dhundhirāja, residing in Vārāṇasī,
whose power is renowned for removing the threefold afflictions,
the sole ground for the birth of the family of the sprouts of bliss!
May you eternally bring a beautiful dawn to the entire world. 4.
Whose lotus feet are ever kissed by the meritorious streams of the Ganges water, comparable to the essence of Brahman,
and who is attended in the midst by all the hosts of immortals;
O Śrī Kāśī, grant perpetual auspicious dawn upon the earth! 5.
With multitudes of ancient, innumerable monasteries, temples, holy fords, reservoirs, palaces, and ghats, as well as with the most eminent scholars,
you constantly captivate the minds of the entire world.
O Śrī Kāśī, grant perpetual auspicious dawn upon the earth! 6.
Which men indeed— whether wise, foolish, or even those lacking intellect— would not desire Your refuge at the time of death?
O You who are expert in bestowing liberation upon millions upon millions of beings!
O Śrī Kāśī, grant perpetual auspicious dawn upon this earth! 7.
She who is resorted to for the sake of spiritual perfection by gods, asuras, sons of the lords of sages, gandharvas, yakṣas, uragas, nāgas, inhabitants of the earth, and the best of the twice-born;
she who is surrounded by innumerable sacred bathing places on the banks of the north-flowing Gaṅgā.
May that Kāśī, the royal city of the enemy of Tripura, grant constant auspiciousness. 8.
The most excellent of holy fords, the fulfiller of desires, the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence,
she who is attended by hosts of Nandas, Ānandis, and Gaṇeśvaras, and praised by all the gods;
she who is the singular jewel-earring of Śambhu and the long pond of Viṣṇu’s asceticism.
May this divine Śrī Maṇikarṇikā always bestow auspiciousness. 9.
This fresh vine of poison, a garland of *mālatī* flowers upon the head of Viṣṇu— the lotus-footed crusher of Madana—
is a certain victory-banner of the Goddess of Liberation; may she be victorious!
May the Ganges, who has washed away the stain of strife, purify us. 10.
May the enchanting water of the Ganges, fallen from the feet of Murāri, flowing upon the head of Tripurāri, and destroying all sins, purify me. 11.
Hanging from the great cheeks of Gaṇeśa, who causes the dwelling of obstacles to cease;
whose serpent-like luster is surpassed by the mass of moonbeams reddened by vermilion;
the beloved of the illustrious Viśveśvara, who is joyfully delighted by the Daughter of the Mountain.
May the joyful Dhundhirāja, with a smiling face, always grant you auspiciousness. 12.
The Lord Śrī Viśvanātha, who bears the shimmering, terrible poison upon his throat, the waters of the Gaṅgā upon his head,
and the virtuous Bhavānī, daughter of the King of Mountains, as his consort on his left side,
accompanied by Nandin, Skanda, and the lords of the Gaṇas— [to him I bow].
May the Teacher of All, residing in the temple of Kāśī, ever bestow auspiciousness. 13.
O Śrī Viśvanātha, ocean filled with the nectar of compassion,
whose auspicious crest is adorned by a fragment of the moon;
arise for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all people!
May you eternally bring a beautiful dawn to the entire world. 14.
O Śrī Viśvanātha, whose banner is the bull, who are worshipped by the universe, the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution, God of gods;
O you whose lotus feet are beyond the reach of words and praised by the great seers!
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 15.
O Śrī Viśvanātha, destroyer of worldly existence, possessor of divine nature,
bearer of the Gaṅgā, praised by the Pramathas, you of beautiful form, adorned with a necklace of lordly serpents, remover of the fear of prostrate devotees!
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 16.
O Śrī Viśvanātha, I bow eternally to Your pair of feet; O Śiva, I remember Your very name within my heart;
O Sinless One, I adorn my speech with Your glory alone.
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 17.
O you whose lotus feet are served by sages dwelling in Kāśī,
whose mass of matted hair is sprinkled by the flood of the waters of the Gaṅgā— [salutations] to you,
the cause of this entire world with its mobile and immobile beings.
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 18.

O beloved of the daughter of the mountain who bears the Gaṅgā, O peaceful-formed one, O you who are known through the Vedānta, O Lord of all, O you whose form is the universe! O immutable and eternal one, O you whose fame is sung in all the scriptures!
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 19.
Today this entire universe has fallen into dense, delusive darkness and has reached a state of insentience; therefore,
O You of unfailing power, illumine it with Your supreme radiance.
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 20.
His son is skilled in destroying the obstacles of all people;
his wife is constantly devoted to giving food to those in need;
and he himself is renowned as one who, having been favored by Śiva, bestows all desired objects upon supplicants.
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 21.
For those men who do not bow, do not recite, do not acknowledge, nor speak, lament, or offer prayers— their intellects being like those of ignorant children— [for them...]
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 22.
O Śrīkaṇṭha, whose neck bears serpents, O Blue-throated One, whose presence is sought by throngs of longing devotees,
whose entire body is resplendent with the ash-smeared cosmetic!
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 23.
O beloved of Śrī Pārvatī’s heart, five-faced one,
illustrious Nīlakaṇṭha, adorned with a garland of human skulls;
O Śrī Viśvanātha, whose feet are as lovely as tender lotuses!
O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, grant a beautiful dawn! 24.
To him whose beautiful waves are like streams of milk, whose assembly of devotees is purified by the flow of merit,
and whose lotus feet are constantly served by ascetics;
O Gaṅgā, you who grant refuge and bestow auspiciousness, grant a beautiful dawn. 25.
I take refuge in Śrī Viśvanātha, the Lord of Vārāṇasī, the protector of the helpless, the root of bliss who dwells joyfully in Ānandavana, and who has destroyed the multitude of sins. 26.
Thus ends "The Auspicious Dawn of Viśvanātha of Kāśī."
